method.rationale: Adaptive two-frontier search is a distinct alternative for hunts without a trustworthy finite census: expand both predicates cheaply, then allocate spend by marginal verified yield rather than committing to one anchor.
method.instructions: Translate X and Y into precise eligibility tests, including exclusions and time boundaries. Maintain two deduplicated candidate frontiers, one surfaced from X and one from Y, plus a ledger of verified, rejected, and unresolved identities. Begin with one search focused on each predicate and one conjunction search, sequentially so results inform the next query. Cross-match the frontiers, but verify identity and both conditions rather than treating name overlap as proof. Alternate short discovery and check_candidates rounds. Partition discovery by source, subtype, geography, era, or alphabet only where meaningful; include less obvious eligible subtypes rather than repeatedly rephrasing a successful query. Measure newly verified items per spend and new plausible candidates per search. Favor the more productive frontier while keeping a small reverse-side gap check. After two searches add no plausible candidates, change partition, provider, or frontier instead of repeating. Keep at least 35% of the initial budget for checking and evidence resolution; stop discovery earlier if the pending queue needs it. Submit only evidenced intersections, deduplicated at the hunt's entity level; do not claim completeness from search saturation alone.
method.routing_rules: Run baseline discovery on Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results. Use Exa alone for batched check_candidates, explicitly requesting both eligibility tests and identity-matched evidence. Once baseline frontiers are sampled, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if affordable; retain it for further discovery only if it adds useful candidates or unique evidence. Compare marginal outcomes, recognizing provider attribution is overlapping and the initial yield sample is small. Use Parallel for cheap exact-name follow-ups and Exa for consequential unresolved checks; do not repeat settled checks. Budget every variant separately and never trigger broad auto-routing. Exact checks may use 4 results; discovery remains at 8. Apply authoritative-domain filters to evidence checks, not the entire discovery frontier. Use date filters only when logically appropriate, not as a substitute for checking event or effective dates.
method.fetch_policy: Fetch only when summaries leave material eligibility or identity uncertain, or when a discovered list offers several new candidates. Prioritize pages likely to resolve multiple candidates and authoritative evidence for near-complete cases. Cache source facts and URLs, avoid fetching every hit, and abandon low-information fetch chains in favor of a targeted alternate-source search.

summary.notes: Two supported recipients: Graham Patera (https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/2235) and Danilova crater (https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/1401) are IAU-adopted Venus features. The original Graham crater name was dropped and replaced by Graham Patera; Danilova crater is named jointly for Maria and Alexandra Danilova. The Kennedy Center and IAU give different birth years for Alexandra, but both identify the same Russian-American ballerina who died in 1997.

conditions.x: How many Kennedy Center Honors recipients have an IAU-approved surface feature on Venus named after them? Count each person once. Use IAU names in force as of November 2026. List each person.

failure_links.why: The successful attempt still committed 0.018 to an eighteen-name first-pass batch, illustrating the existing per-candidate cost concentration. This is an opportunity for interruptible allocation, not evidence of missed finds.

candidates.rationale: Interruptible cohort sampling: retain adaptive dual frontiers and the cheap verification cascade, but replace long speculative candidate batches with small feedback-driven samples. Unlike census-first, source-bundle allocation, or a final evidence audit, this changes when verification commitments are made. Parallel's observed 163.8 correct/dollar versus Exa's 60.7 supports cheap sampling, not a causal accuracy claim. The successful train trace spent 0.018 on one eighteen-name batch; sampling could redirect that spend earlier when a cohort is unproductive. This remains an untested improvement hypothesis.
candidates.instructions: Define both predicates precisely, including entity unit, eligible subtypes, exclusions and effective dates. Start sequentially with one X search, one Y search and one conjunction search. Maintain deduplicated dual frontiers and a ledger of canonical identities, aliases, evidence for each predicate, unresolved facts and estimated next-action cost. Group pending candidates into meaningful cohorts by their discovery source or eligibility subtype; do not invent arbitrary cohorts when none are useful. Separate evidence-backed near-intersections from speculative candidates that satisfy only one predicate. Resolve near-intersections first. For a speculative cohort, check at most three diverse candidates before committing more spend, and limit each dispatch to 10% of the initial budget; a single necessary check may exceed that cap if affordable. Inspect returned evidence before dispatching another sample. If a sample yields no verified addition or materially improved evidence, park that cohort and test another partition or the reverse frontier. No-hit candidates remain unresolved, not rejected. Revisit a parked cohort when new evidence, an alias or a demonstrably different source gives a better resolution path; a failed sample never proves the cohort empty. Expand productive cohorts in similarly small rounds, comparing verified additions and evidence progress per actual spend against discovery alternatives. Retain one neglected-cohort or reverse-frontier probe after two productive rounds so early samples do not permanently starve rare subtypes. After two discovery queries add no plausible identities, change source, subtype or frontier rather than paraphrasing the conjunction. Reuse established facts and never repeat settled checks. Keep at least 35% of initial budget for verification and evidence resolution, and stop discovery earlier if the promising pending queue requires it. End with identity, scope and date checks; submit only individually supported intersections and do not infer completeness from sampling or search saturation.
candidates.routing_rules: Use Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for discovery and 4 for exact-name checks and first-pass check_candidates. Request identity-matched evidence for both tests while directing retrieval to the missing fact. Estimate dispatch cost per candidate and provider, not per tool invocation; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Escalate only individual promising unresolved cases to Exa alone with 4 results after a cheap check or targeted fetch fails; never escalate a whole cohort because one member is ambiguous. Following baseline sampling and genuine Parallel stagnation, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if the resolution reserve remains intact; retain Exa discovery only for useful incremental evidence or identities. No broad auto-routing or routine concurrent variants. Domain filters belong on targeted evidence checks, with relaxation when necessary, not the entire discovery frontier. Use publication-date filters only when publication date defines eligibility; check effective dates in source content.
candidates.fetch_policy: Cache facts and URLs. Fetch when source content can resolve a material identity or predicate uncertainty, or a discovered list supplies several plausible candidates. Prefer authoritative pages and shared evidence that reduces pending-check cost, without turning source bundles into the mandatory discovery unit. Do not fetch every result. After a blocked or uninformative page, try one targeted alternate source rather than a fetch chain.
